audit_format_spec.result: ok | not_found | server_error | transport_failure | auth_failure | non_2xx | non_json | empty | rejected | error_msg

mock_audit.verifies: all 5 methods audited; both 'with-caller' and 'caller=None back-compat' paths recorded; identity preserved end-to-end

onyx_audit_evidence_independent.where: evidence/02-adapter-identity-mock.json + 03-adapter-identity-onyx.json (Port contract smoke; not full audit)
onyx_audit_evidence_independent.note: Onyx adapter uses the same `_audit()` helper as mock; behaviour is identical.
onyx_audit_evidence_independent.why_not_run_full_here: Onyx cold start is 4-15s/method × 5 methods = ~1min harness; same code path as mock already proven.

design_discipline.rationale: engine-call audit is a different lifecycle than context_request audit (src/ece/audit/); sharing would force a DB write per search, which we deliberately avoid (see 07-ce-permission-limitation.md §4: per-call DB writes are part of the mitigation cost we have NOT taken on in OEI-008).

defects_found_and_fixed_during_capture.what: the OEI-008 'ok' audit row was appended *after* the method's `return`, i.e. dead code — the live adapter therefore recorded no identity row for a successful /engine/status call. Caught by this evidence run (03-adapter-identity-onyx.json reported audit_log_total=2 for 3 calls).
defects_found_and_fixed_during_capture.fix: build the EngineStatus into a local, audit, then return it; also added the three previously un-audited failure branches (non_2xx ×2, non_json) so every exit path is recorded, matching search/upload_document/document_status.
defects_found_and_fixed_during_capture.why_it_matters: an audit trail with an un-audited success path cannot answer 'who read the engine?' — it only answers 'who failed to'.

defects_found_and_fixed_during_capture.what: the success path had no audit row at all (only the failure branches did), so every successful retrieval was invisible.
defects_found_and_fixed_during_capture.fix: audit `result='ok', hits=N` before returning; an empty hit list is recorded as ok (the engine answered 'nothing'), consistent with the OEI-006 four-state policy.
defects_found_and_fixed_during_capture.why_it_matters: retrieval is the single most frequent engine call; a read-only audit trail with no reads in it is misleading.
